newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee ends steady in spot, weakens in fwd.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee ends steady in spot, weakens in fwd.

text.p: The Indian rupee ended Wednesday at 35.790/795 per dollar, unchanged from Tuesday's close but marginally up from opening quotes of 35.795/80, dealers said.
They said the rupee remained steady despite Reserve Bank of India (RBI) spot dollar purchases.
"RBI bought in the afternoon but in limited amounts," said a dealer at a foreign bank. "They would have bought $30-50 million today."
The dealer said dollar supply was strong enough to absorb RBI purchases and the rupee remained steady.
"The State Bank of India also bought in the afternoon but even the combined buying (along with RBI) did not affect the rupee much," he said.
Dealers said they expected the rupee to remain strong against the dollar in the short term on good supply and poor demand.
"If the rupee is to weaken, the RBI has to buy aggressively," said another dealer. "At the moment, it is more a mopping-up operation than intervention in the real sense."
Dealers said the rupee opened down against the forward dollar on fears of a tightening in domestic liquidity next week.
The RBI auctions 30 billion rupees of three-year federal government bonds on May 28.

"Forward premiums opened up as there was a fear call money will tighten on outflows towards the bond auction," said a dealer. "But there was profit-taking at higher levels and premiums ended only slightly above Tuesday's close."
Dealers said demand and supply of forward dollars remained well-matched, with most demand coming from banks which were rolling over swaps.
"Unless import demand comes in, and that will be only if the rupee falls to around 35.90, six-month forward premiums will remain in a 4.5-5.0 percent range," said a dealer.
The annualised premium for six-month dollars ended Wednesday at 4.75 percent against Tuesday's 4.58 percent.
